item.title: AI Usage Tracker: Local-First, Privacy-Focused Tool for Tracking AI Coding Costs
item.description:
AI Usage Tracker: Local-First, Privacy-Focused Tool for Tracking AI Coding Costs

AI Usage Tracker, formerly Claude Usage Tracker, is a local-first tool that automatically discovers and aggregates your AI coding usage across 10+ development tools — covering both Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex.

🔍 Overview

It scans known data directories, parses JSONL/log files, calculates costs using model-specific pricing, and presents everything in a beautiful dark-themed interactive dashboard powered by Chart.js.

🧩 How it works

  • Auto‑discovery detects Claude and Codex tools.
  • Parses JSONL/log files from supported tools.
  • Calculates costs per token using model‑specific pricing.
  • Displays top‑level stats (Today / Week / Month / All‑time / Sessions).

⚙️ Key details

  • Top‑level All / Claude / Codex pill toggle scopes entire dashboard to a single provider.
  • No cloud, no telemetry, no accounts; everything stays on your machine.
  • Cost grouped by working directory to show which projects burn through token budget.
  • Filters by source, model, date range, and minimum cost.
  • Day‑by‑day session timeline with expandable rows and color‑coded model chips.
  • Hourly × day activity grid revealing most productive and expensive coding hours.
  • Drill into any session: token breakdown, conversation preview, one‑click resume command (claude –resume / codex resume ).

#AIUsage #Privacy #DeveloperTools #CostTracking

Source: 658jjh/claude-usage-tracker Source: mostly-ai/mostlyai

item.title: Bitbybit Releases Open-Source TypeScript Monorepo for 3D CAD Algorithms with AI Integration
item.description:
Bitbybit Releases Open-Source TypeScript Monorepo for 3D CAD Algorithms with AI Integration

Bitbybit has released a new open-source monorepo that provides TypeScript implementations of 3D CAD algorithms for browser-based geometry programming. The repository contains all Bitbybit NPM packages along with example applications under MIT license, enabling developers to work with 3D algorithms using popular frameworks like ThreeJS, BabylonJS, and PlayCanvas. The monorepo supports both direct algorithm execution in NodeJS and custom core integrations, making it a versatile foundation for 3D geometry development. The project includes three CAD kernels (OCCT, JSCAD, Manifold) and offers a CLI that generates Vite + TypeScript projects pre-configured with these kernels, allowing developers to choose between different game engines and backend templates while keeping API keys secure on the server side.

#TypeScript #3D #CAD #WebAssembly #Monorepo #AI

Source: bitbybit-dev/bitbybit

item.title: Pydantic AI Skills Enhances Agent Capabilities with Progressive Disclosure
item.description:
Pydantic AI Skills Enhances Agent Capabilities with Progressive Disclosure

Pydantic AI Skills introduces enhanced capabilities for Agent Skills, supporting progressive disclosure and modular packages of instructions, resources, and scripts. This update allows agents to handle specialized tasks more efficiently by loading only the necessary resources when needed.

🔍 Overview

  • Pydantic AI Skills enhances Agent Skills with progressive disclosure.
  • Supports filesystem and programmatic skills.
  • Enables remote skill registries and bundled-file execution.

🧩 How it works

  • Agent Skills are modular packages of instructions, resources, and scripts.
  • On disk, a skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file, reference documents, and executable scripts.
  • Your agent starts with only the name and description of each skill.
  • When a task calls for a skill, it loads the full instructions and resources only if needed.
  • This is progressive disclosure, allowing the skill library to grow without every skill paying for space in the prompt.

⚙️ Key details

  • pydantic-ai-harness ships a Skills capability that reads SKILL.md packages from local directories.
  • pydantic-ai-skills is the companion that fills the gaps, including remote registries and bundled-file execution.
  • Remote registries support Git and S3 sources, with composition features.
  • Bundled files can be read or executed with read_skill_resource and run_skill_script.
  • Sandboxed execution keeps untrusted scripts off the host.
  • ${SKILL_DIR} resolution substitutes the path in scripts.
  • Programmatic skills can be defined in Python within the same catalog.
  • v2 introduces SkillsToolset, SkillsDirectory, reload(), and tools for listing and loading skills.
  • Each skill becomes its own deferred capability, with names and descriptions acting as fields the runtime uses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Progressive disclosure allows the skill library to grow without every skill paying for space in the prompt.
  • Enhanced capabilities for handling specialized tasks more efficiently.
  • Supports remote skill registries and bundled-file execution.
  • Sandboxed execution ensures security for untrusted scripts.

#PydanticAI #AgentSkills #ProgressiveDisclosure #AIAgents #AITools

Source: DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills

item.title: Prefect Team Offers FastMCP Framework and Gateway for Model Context Protocol
item.description:
Prefect Team Offers FastMCP Framework and Gateway for Model Context Protocol

The Prefect team has developed FastMCP, a full Model Context Protocol (MCP) application framework that connects Large Language Models (LLMs) to tools and data. To support team-wide scaling, the team also provides FastMCP Gateway, an enterprise gateway for deploying, securing, and governing MCP servers and tools.

🔍 Overview

FastMCP handles the application layer of the Model Context Protocol, simplifying what is otherwise a complex development process. Since its inception, FastMCP 1.0 was incorporated into the official MCP Python SDK in 2024. Today, FastMCP is an actively maintained standalone project downloaded a million times a day, and some version of FastMCP powers 70% of MCP servers across all languages.

🧩 How it works

FastMCP automates the tedious parts of building MCP applications and operates on three primary pillars:

Pillar Description
Servers Wrap your Python functions into MCP-compliant tools, resources, and prompts.
Clients Connect to any server with full protocol support.
Apps Give your tools interactive UIs rendered directly in the conversation.

By managing the application layer, FastMCP handles several tasks automatically:

  • Tool Declaration: Declare a tool using a Python function, and the schema, validation, and documentation are generated automatically.
  • Server Connection: Connect to a server with a URL, and FastMCP manages transport negotiation, authentication, and the protocol lifecycle.

To build a server, developers start with ordinary Python. It is recommended to add FastMCP to your project with uv. For comprehensive instructions, including verification and upgrading, see the Installation Guide.

⚙️ Key details

FastMCP and its enterprise extension offer several capabilities for developers and organizations:

  • Cross-Language Support: In addition to Python, FastMCP for TypeScript is the official counterpart, built and maintained by the same team.
  • Enterprise Scaling: FastMCP Gateway allows teams to deploy FastMCP servers from GitHub with branch previews and instant rollback, create private registries of company-wide MCPs, and secure access with SSO and tool-level RBAC.
  • Observability and Governance: FastMCP Gateway provides centralized governance, audit logs, and observability across your MCP stack, allowing teams to remix approved tools into purpose-built endpoints for teams and agents.

#ModelContextProtocol #FastMCP #Python #TypeScript #Prefect

Source: PrefectHQ/fastmcp

item.title: Databricks launches Genie Migrate for Serverless to automate classic-to-serverless migration
item.description:
Databricks launches Genie Migrate for Serverless to automate classic-to-serverless migration

Databricks has launched Genie Migrate for Serverless in beta, an agent that automates the migration of jobs and notebooks from classic compute to serverless compute. The agent handles configuration translation and presents changes as reviewable diffs, reducing migration from a manual research project to a review-and-approve step.

🔍 Overview

  • Serverless compute in Databricks removes the operational burden of managing infrastructure, automatically handling provisioning, scaling, and optimization.
  • Serverless usage has grown multifold in the past year, with thousands of customers running notebooks and jobs on it.
  • Most teams still have classic fleets they want to migrate to gain cost and operational benefits.
  • Manual migration has been difficult: flipping a job to serverless often produces errors, access-mode incompatibilities, Spark config issues, or missing libraries.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent runs from the /compute migrate slash command inside Genie on any job or notebook.
  • It is fully managed and requires no setup to start scanning.
  • Because Databricks manages it, the agent reads your job config and workload code inside your own workspace.
  • Before any changes, the agent scans your Jobs and Notebooks and marks each workload with its serverless readiness.
  • Once you pick an eligible workload, the agent proposes the changes needed for serverless and presents them for review before anything is written.
  • Nothing is applied until you approve it.
  • Every change, including code rewrites, is presented as a reviewable diff with a side-by-side comparison.
  • If the agent is unsure about something (for example, whether a Spark conf is still needed), it reports the conf rather than removing it.
  • For a larger fleet, you can run Genie Migrate for Serverless in the background with the Databricks CLI.
  • Your original job does not change until you review and approve its migration, and approving keeps the job’s ID, schedule, and permissions.

⚙️ Key details

Aspect Detail
Launch status Beta
Invocation /compute migrate slash command in Genie
Setup required None (fully managed)
Scope Jobs and notebooks inside the workspace
External sources Not supported yet (e.g., Databricks Asset Bundles, Git folders)
Change application Only after explicit approval
Diff presentation Side-by-side comparison of what will change and what will not
Uncertainty handling Reports Spark confs rather than removing them
Validation today Deterministic checks for correctness
Validation coming Deeper runtime validation in isolated sandbox against classic baseline
Fleet migration Background runs via Databricks CLI
Job identity preserved Job ID, schedule, and permissions retained after approval

🚀 Availability

  • Genie Migrate for Serverless is available now in beta.
  • No setup is required; the agent runs from within Genie in your workspace.
  • Background fleet scanning and migration are supported via the Databricks CLI.

💡 Why it matters

  • Moves the translation knowledge from the practitioner’s head and trial-and-error onto the platform.
  • Turns workload migration into a review-and-approve step rather than a research project.
  • Keeps judgment with the user: whether to migrate now, whether proposed changes look right, and whether the migrated run is healthy.
  • Provides an explicit contract (side-by-side diff) that can be handed to a manager or on-call rotation.
  • Is honest about what it has and has not proven, with runtime validation coming to show correctness signals before apply.

#Databricks #Serverless #Migration #Genie #DataEngineering #AI

Source: Introducing Genie Migrate for Serverless

item.title: Rigging: A Lightweight LLM Framework for Production
item.description:
Rigging: A Lightweight LLM Framework for Production

Rigging is a lightweight LLM framework designed to simplify the use of language models in production code. It integrates with various models and offers features like structured Pydantic models, LiteLLM as the default generator, and async batching for large-scale generation.

🔍 Overview

  • Rigging is built by dreadnode and is used daily in their operations.
  • It supports a wide range of models including those from LiteLLM, vLLM, and transformers.
  • The framework allows for the definition of prompts as Python functions with type hints and docstrings.
  • It includes simple tool use and integrated tracing support with Logfire.

⚙️ Key details

  • Rigging can be installed via pip: pip install rigging.
  • Models and configs are stored as simple connection strings, similar to databases.
  • API keys can be passed in a generator ID or through standard environment variables.
  • Rigging supports both chat and completion pipelines.

🚀 Availability

  • Rigging is available for use and documentation can be found at docs.dreadnode.io.
  • Example scripts include basic interactive chat, Jupyter code interpreter, OverTheWire Bandit Agent, Damn Vulnerable Restaurant Agent, and RAG Pipeline.

💡 Why it matters

  • Rigging makes using language models in production code simpler and more effective.
  • It supports modern Python features like type hints, async support, and Pydantic validation.
  • The framework allows for fast iterations and large-scale generation.

item.title: SD Prompt Reader Available as ComfyUI Node and Desktop App
item.description:
SD Prompt Reader Available as ComfyUI Node and Desktop App

A simple standalone viewer for reading prompt from Stable Diffusion generated image outside the webui. The SD Prompt Reader is now available as a ComfyUI node.

🔍 Overview

The SD Prompt Reader provides both GUI and CLI. It allows you to perform the following actions:

  • Simple drag and drop interaction
  • Copy prompt to clipboard
  • Remove prompt from image
  • Export prompt to text file
  • Edit or import prompt to images

Vertical orientation display and sorting by alphabet are also included. Dark and light mode support is provided. For desktop builds from current source, see Building desktop applications. For Windows users, Download executable from GitHub Releases. For macOS users, Download executable from GitHub Releases. You may also install SD Prompt Reader via Homebrew cask. brew install –no-quarantine

🚀 Availability

RuinedFooocus PNG support is available in the development version only (#77). If you are using a tool or format that is not on this list, please help me to support your format by uploading the original file generated by your tool to the issues, thx.

item.title: Attu 3.0 Expands AI-Native Management for Milvus Vector Databases
item.description:
Attu 3.0 Expands AI-Native Management for Milvus Vector Databases

Attu 3.0, an AI-native management tool for Milvus vector databases, has been released, expanding the visual experience for Milvus 3.0 while retaining compatibility with Milvus 2.6.0+ and Zilliz Cloud.

🔍 Overview

  • Attu is an AI-native management tool for Milvus vector databases.
  • Connect to multiple Milvus clusters from a single instance, browse collections, run vector searches, manage backups, monitor health, and chat with an AI agent that understands your data.

🚀 Availability

  • Available as a web app (Docker, Kubernetes, or a standalone server package) or desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows).
  • Attu v3.0 supports Zilliz Cloud and open-source Milvus 2.6.0+ and 3.x.
  • Milvus 2.5.x and earlier are not supported.
  • The v3.0.0 release includes a non-Docker, non-Electron server package for Linux x64.

⚙️ Key details

  • Explore Parquet and Iceberg data without copying it into Milvus, refresh external schemas and data, and browse or restore Collection Snapshots.
  • Work with Milvus TEXT fields, add or remove supported fields, edit descriptions, and manage Function Fields from the Schema page.
  • Run Query and Search aggregations, group and order results, paginate large result sets, and apply Function Score reranking.
  • Configure MinHash Function Fields and MINHASH_LSH indexes to find near-duplicate documents from raw text.
  • Register reusable dictionaries, stop-word lists, synonym lists, and tokenizer resources.
  • Load or release individual partitions, configure entity-level TTL, export complete Collections, and import large files in chunks.
  • The Docker image stores its SQLite database at /data/attu.db by default.
  • The -v attu-data:/data volume persists your saved connections, agent conversations, and preferences across container restarts.
  • The image runs as the non-root node user (uid=1000, gid=1000), so named volumes are recommended.
  • On SELinux-enabled hosts, also add the :Z mount option: ./attu-data:/data:Z.
  • The non-Docker server package requires Node.js 24.x and includes the Attu server bundle and bin/milvus-backup.
  • The launcher defaults to 0.0.0.0:3080.
  • Set HOST, PORT, ATTU_DATA_DIR, or ATTU_DB_PATH to customize the runtime paths and listener.
  • Connect to multiple Milvus instances from a single Attu deployment.
  • Add, edit, and switch between connections in the sidebar.
  • Each cluster has its own dedicated workspace with independent monitoring, agent sessions, and preferences, ideal for managing dev, staging, and production environments side by side.
  • Browse databases and collections, view and edit data inline, import/export in CSV, JSON, and Parquet formats.
  • Interactive vector similarity search with configurable embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Jina, VoyageAI, and more).

#Milvus #VectorDatabases #AIManagement #Attu #DataScience

Source: zilliztech/attu

item.title: Chandra OCR 2: Advanced Document Conversion and Extraction
item.description:
Chandra OCR 2: Advanced Document Conversion and Extraction

Chandra OCR 2, a state-of-the-art OCR model, has been released with significant improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR. It converts images and PDFs into structured HTML/Markdown/JSON while preserving layout information.

🔍 Overview

  • Chandra OCR 2 is a state-of-the-art OCR model that converts images and PDFs into structured HTML/Markdown/JSON while preserving layout information.
  • It has significant improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR.
  • The model supports 90+ languages and has excellent handwriting support.
  • It reconstructs forms accurately, including checkboxes, and has strong performance with tables, math, and complex layouts.
  • The model extracts images and diagrams, and adds captions and structured data.

⚙️ Key details

  • Chandra OCR 2 has two inference modes: local (HuggingFace) and remote (vLLM server).
  • Multilingual performance was a focus for Chandra 2. There isn’t a good public multilingual OCR benchmark, so the team made their own.
  • The model was benchmarked with the widely accepted olmocr benchmark.

🚀 Availability

  • Chandra OCR 2 is available for commercial self-hosting with a license.
  • For on-prem licensing, contact the team.
  • The Datalab API turns documents into verifiable knowledge your agents act on. Every result traces back to its page and position, and one API can parse, extract, fill and edit documents.
  • Get started with about 5,000 free convert pages every month (work email) — sign up — takes under 30 seconds — or try Chandra in the public playground.
  • If you have high volume workloads, a batch processing service is available that has processed 1B+ pages in a day at peak.

💡 Why it matters

  • Chandra OCR 2’s improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR make it a powerful tool for document conversion and extraction.
  • The model’s ability to preserve layout information and reconstruct forms accurately is particularly notable.
  • The availability of a batch processing service for high volume workloads ensures that users can manage their workloads efficiently.

📦 Installation 

1

pip install chandra-ocr

🔧 Usage

  • With vLLM (recommended, lightweight install)
1

chandra input.pdf ./output
  • Print Markdown directly to stdout
1

chandra input.pdf --stdout
  • With HuggingFace (requires torch + transformers)
1
2

pip install "chandra-ocr[hf]"
chandra input.pdf ./output --method hf
  • Interactive Web Viewer (zero extra dependencies)
1

chandra_app

📅 Timeline

  • 3/2026 - Chandra 2 is here with significant improvements to math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR
  • 10/2025 - Chandra 1 launched

🌐 Multilingual Performance

  • The model supports 90+ languages.
  • Multilingual performance was a focus for Chandra 2.
  • The team made their own multilingual OCR benchmark to test tables, math, ordering, layout, and text accuracy.

📊 Benchmarks

  • Tops external olmocr benchmark and significant improvement in internal multilingual benchmarks.

📄 Document Conversion

  • Convert documents to markdown, html, or json with detailed layout information.

📝 Document Extraction

  • Extracts images and diagrams, and adds captions and structured data.

📋 Form Reconstruction

  • Reconstructs forms accurately, including checkboxes.

📝 Handwriting Support

  • Excellent handwriting support.

📊 Table Performance

  • Strong performance with tables, math, and complex layouts.

#OCR #DocumentConversion #AI #MachineLearning #DataExtraction

item.title: MCP Appium Empowers AI Assistants with Mobile Automation
item.description:
MCP Appium Empowers AI Assistants with Mobile Automation

MCP Appium is an intelligent MCP (Model Context Protocol) server designed to empower AI assistants with a robust suite of tools for mobile automation.

🔍 Overview

  • MCP Appium streamlines mobile app testing by enabling natural language interactions, intelligent locator generation, and automated test creation for both Android and iOS platforms.

🧩 How it works

  • Automate tests for both Android (UiAutomator2) and iOS (XCUITest).
  • Locate UI elements using natural language descriptions powered by vision models - no need for complex XPath or selectors.
  • AI-powered element identification using priority-based strategies.
  • Easily create and manage sessions on local mobile devices.
  • Perform actions like clicks, text input, screenshots, and element finding.
  • Generate Java/TestNG test code from natural language descriptions.
  • Utilize built-in templates that follow industry best practices.
  • Customize capabilities and settings for different environments.
  • Use your native language - AI handles all interactions naturally in any language (English, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.).

⚙️ Key details

  • Ensure you have the following installed: Node.js (v22 or higher), npm or yarn, Java Development Kit (JDK) (8 or higher), Android SDK (for Android testing), Xcode (for iOS testing on macOS).
  • MCP Appium supports two driver modes: Embedded local drivers and Remote WebDriver/Appium server.

🚀 Availability

  • Install Android Studio and the Android SDK.
  • Set the ANDROID_HOME environment variable.
  • Add the Android SDK tools to your system’s PATH.
  • Enable USB debugging on your Android device.
  • Install the Android platform tools/build tools and keep adb available on PATH.
  • Install Xcode from the App Store.
  • Install the Xcode Command Line Tools: xcode-select –install.
  • Install iOS simulators through Xcode.
  • For real device testing, enable Developer Mode on the device and sign in to your Apple ID in Xcode (Settings → Accounts).
  • Use appium_prepare_ios_real_device to download and sign WebDriverAgent in a single call - it will guide you through provisioning profile selection and return capabilities for session startup.
  • Standard config works in most of the tools.
  • The easiest way to install MCP Appium in Cursor IDE is using the one-click install button.
  • This will automatically configure the MCP server in your Cursor IDE settings.
  • Make sure to update the ANDROID_HOME environment variable in the configuration to match your Android SDK path.
  • Go to Cursor Settings → MCP → Add new MCP Server.
  • Name it to your liking, use command type with the command npx -y appium-mcp@latest.
  • You can also verify config or add command arguments via clicking Edit.
  • Here is the recommended configuration:
  • Make sure to update the ANDROID_HOME path to match your Android SDK installation path.
  • The –httpStream transport rejects MCP requests containing an Origin header by default and disables CORS.

💡 Why it matters

  • MCP Appium simplifies mobile app testing by leveraging natural language interactions and AI-powered element identification, making it easier to create and manage automated tests for both Android and iOS platforms.

#MCPAppium #MobileAutomation #AIAssistants #AppTesting #MobileDevelopment

Source: appium/appium-mcp

item.title: Milvus Backup: Command-Line Tool for Milvus Data Management
item.description:
Milvus Backup: Command-Line Tool for Milvus Data Management

Milvus Backup is a command-line tool and API service for backing up and restoring Milvus data. It allows backup and restore operations to run while the Milvus cluster remains available.

🔍 Overview

  • Milvus Backup is a command-line tool and API service for backing up and restoring Milvus data.
  • Backup and restore operations run while the Milvus cluster remains available.

⚙️ Key details

  • Download a binary from the release page, or install it with Homebrew on macOS:
    • brew install zilliztech/tap/milvus-backup
  • To build from source instead, run make all; the executable is written to ./milvus-backup.
  • Milvus Backup reads its connection settings from a configuration file.
  • Copy the example and update it for your deployment — Configuration explains what to change:
    • cp configs/backup.yaml backup.yaml
  • Then validate the setup and run your first backup and restore:
    • milvus-backup check
    • milvus-backup create -n my_backup
    • milvus-backup list
    • milvus-backup restore -n my_backup

🚀 Availability

  • The latest version supports backups from Milvus 2.2 and later, and restores to Milvus 2.5 and later.
  • A backup can be restored only to the same or a newer Milvus version.

💡 Why it matters

  • Milvus Backup allows for the management of Milvus data with ease, ensuring data availability and integrity.
  • It supports various commands for different operations, making it a versatile tool for Milvus data management.

#Milvus #Backup #DataManagement #AI #Database

Source: zilliztech/milvus-backup

item.title: MobileBuildMCP Launches AI Development Toolkit for iOS and macOS Projects

item.title: NVIDIA Introduces Open Source SOMA Retargeter for Humanoid Motion Adaptation
item.description:
NVIDIA Introduces Open Source SOMA Retargeter for Humanoid Motion Adaptation

The open source NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter adapts human motion data to fit a humanoid robot’s specific proportions, joint structures, and ranges of motion. Built around the shared human-motion representation in NVIDIA SOMA-X, the tool provides capabilities to configure robot embodiments, refine motion, and process trajectory data for downstream learning or control systems.

⚙️ How It Works

Directly copying human joint movement is not feasible for humanoid robots due to differences in physical structure. SOMA Retargeter adapts motion through a standardized workflow:

  • Input: Reads a Biovision Hierarchy (BVH) animation represented on the SOMA base skeleton.
  • Processing: Scales motion targets to the robot’s proportions, solves configured inverse-kinematics objectives for joint poses per frame, and applies configured post-processing corrections.
  • Output: Generates a comma-separated values (CSV) file containing the robot’s root position, orientation, and joint angles for each frame.

🧩 Compatible Motion Sources

Human motion inputs can be unified on the SOMA skeleton representation across multiple capture and generation methods:

Source / Tool Function Description
BONES-SEED Motion Capture Collection of human motion-capture data.
GEM-X Video Reconstruction Reconstructs whole-body 3D human motion from a single video using the SOMA body model.
Kimodo Motion Generation Generates human motion sequences from text and pose constraints on the SOMA skeleton.
ARDY Motion Generation Generates movement from text and pose constraints with interactive steering as motion unfolds.

🚀 SOMA Retargeter v0.2 Release

The v0.2 release includes sample motions from the BONES-SEED dataset, reference retargeting results, and pre-built configurations for five humanoid robot embodiments:

  • Unitree G1
  • Unitree H2
  • Booster T1
  • AgiBot X2 Ultra
  • AgiBot A3T3

To retarget a sample forward walk using the Unitree G1 configuration, users open a terminal in the repository root and start the viewer:

uv run python app/bvh_to_csv_converter.py --config assets/default_bvh_to_csv_converter_config.json --viewer gl

With unitree_g1 selected by default, selecting Retarget on the BVH Motion row under Scene Options → Motion executes the scaling, inverse-kinematics solving, and post-processing. The viewer displays the resulting robot animation alongside the source human motion.

#NVIDIA #Robotics #SOMARetargeter #HumanoidRobots #OpenSource

Source: Adapt Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: Kiro AI IDE and AWS Transform Enable Repeatable PHP‑to‑Java Migration
item.description:
Kiro AI IDE and AWS Transform Enable Repeatable PHP‑to‑Java Migration

A new AI‑enabled workflow lets teams move mature PHP applications to Java with a measurable, repeatable process.

🔍 Overview

  • “When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling.”
  • “Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi‑step engineering tasks with you in the loop.”
  • “AWS Transform is the AWS agentic AI service for large‑scale migration and modernization, and it now integrates natively with Kiro.”

🧩 How it works

  • “The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight‑phase workflow.”
  • “This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.”
  • “Everything here is packaged as skill files: versioned Markdown capability packages that encode the migration methodology (php-to-java-migration) and the discovery scanner workflow (php-model-discovery).”
  • “The engine is organized around a single principle: one shared brain, many projects.”
  • “At the top is a global .kiro/ layer that every project draws on.”
  • “A shared, global layer under .kiro/ holds two Skills, php-model-discovery (the scanner) and php-to-java-migration (the eight‑phase playbook), plus the core‑workflow.md Steering file.”

⚙️ Key details

  • “Kiro brings an AI agent into your editor to drive a migration step by step.”
  • “Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application.”
  • “Kiro then walks the eight‑phase workflow with explicit approval gates, so you review the discovery manifest, approve the rulebook, and sign off on each phase before the next begins.”
  • “Use Kiro to work through the code first: run the skill on one application, read the generated Java, and run the tests.”
  • “When you want to migrate more, AWS Transform runs the same methodology agentically with review at the checkpoints the skill defines.”
  • “Kiro handles one application at a time and suits first‑of‑a‑kind frameworks.”
  • “AWS Transform runs many applications as parallel jobs.”
  • “Both paths read the same skill files, so every rulebook fix made in Kiro improves the next AWS Transform run, and vice versa.”
  • “The scanner is discover‑models.php, a single‑file, dependency‑free PHP command‑line tool that doesn’t execute the target code.”
  • “It only reads source text as tokens, so it runs against apps of your choice whether its dependencies are installed.”
  • “Each per‑project folder holds its own PHP source, Java output, and spec sub‑folder under .kiro/specs/, so improving the methodology once lets every project inherit the gain.”

🚀 Availability

  • “You start with an open repository, so you can run the engine yourself rather than read about it.”
  • “Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application.”
  • “Through that integration, you can hand AWS Transform the same skill files that govern an interactive Kiro session, so discovery before translation, the parity harness as referee, and ‘fix the loop, not the code’ apply to an autonomous run.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling are achieved by moving to Java.
  • An eight‑phase, parity‑first pipeline guarantees that the Java port matches the original PHP specification before it is accepted.
  • The same skill files power both an interactive, single‑application workflow (Kiro) and a large‑scale, parallel workflow (AWS Transform), ensuring consistency across projects.

#PHP #Java #AI #Migration #AWS

Source: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Granite Timeseries Ensemble provides a zero‑training default forecast recipe
item.description:
Granite Timeseries Ensemble provides a zero‑training default forecast recipe

Granite Timeseries Ensemble (Granite TSFM) introduces a default, zero‑training forecast recipe that combines four pre‑trained models.

🔍 Overview

  • Pre‑trained time‑series models can forecast without training on your dataset, but you still have to choose one.
  • Granite Timeseries Ensemble reduces that choice to a sensible default.
  • The default recipe combines four pre‑trained Granite models with different architectures, each capturing trends, seasonality, and local variation in different ways.

🧩 How it works

  • Two main ensemble recipes are provided:
    • Probabilistic Ensemble (uniform probability pooling)
    • IQR Ensemble (weights based on forecast spread)
  • Both recipes work with each member’s quantile forecasts (default 0.1 – 0.9) and produce a median and quantile forecasts.
  • Probabilistic Ensemble gives each member equal influence, pools quantile forecasts in probability space, and extracts the requested quantiles. No fitting step and no weighting hyperparameters are required.
  • IQR Ensemble approximates each member’s inter‑quartile range from the nearest 25th and 75th percentiles, then weights members inversely to their interval width. Weights vary by sample, target, and horizon step; isotonic regression keeps combined quantiles from crossing. A temperature setting and optional cap let users move weights toward uniform or limit any single member’s influence.

⚙️ Key details

  • Each member returns:
    • result.prediction_outputs – the point forecast.
    • result.quantile_outputs – quantile predictions ranging from 0.1 to 0.9.
  • The 0.1 and 0.9 quantiles define a central forecast interval with nominal 80 % coverage.
  • No retraining and no fitted ensemble weights; simple equal‑weight combinations have historically performed well in point forecasting.
  • The ensemble recipe stores the configuration rather than merged model weights; member checkpoints are downloaded at runtime, so allow extra time for the first run.
  • The recipe and its default Granite members are permissively licensed.
  • Both recipes were evaluated on 97 GIFT‑Eval dataset configurations (see the model card for full details, member checkpoints, evaluation, and limitations).

🚀 Availability

  • Install the package with: 
    1

    pip install "granite-tsfm>=0.3.11"
  • Load the recommended four‑model recipe directly from Hugging Face.
  • The model card provides the full configuration, member checkpoints, evaluation details, and known limitations.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a ready‑to‑use, zero‑training forecast solution for a wide range of series, from smooth industrial signals to noisy retail demand.
  • Reduces the risk of selecting a poor single model by combining diverse architectures; a 50‑year review of forecast combinations notes that such ensembles can lower error risk when members are high‑quality and diverse.
  • Enables applications to use the median as a central prediction and selected quantiles to express forecast uncertainty without any hyperparameter tuning.

#TimeSeries #Forecasting #Ensemble #Granite

Source: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models

item.title: Graphify Launches Knowledge Graph Mapping for AI Coding Assistants
item.description:
Graphify Launches Knowledge Graph Mapping for AI Coding Assistants

Graphify has introduced a tool that converts codebases, including documentation, SQL schemas, configurations, and PDFs, into queryable knowledge graphs.

🔍 Overview

Graphify provides a /graphify skill for AI coding assistants including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI. It maps projects—including code, docs, PDFs, images, and videos—into a knowledge graph that users can query as an alternative to grepping through files.

🧩 How it works

Graphify uses different processing methods based on the file type:

File Type Processing Method
Code Local deterministic AST parsing via tree-sitter (no LLM)
Docs, PDFs, Images, Video Assistant’s model or configured API key for a semantic pass

⚙️ Key details

  • Non-Vector Based: The tool is not a vector index and uses no embeddings or vector stores.
  • Local Processing: Code maps are free and fully local; no code leaves the machine during AST parsing.
  • Edge Transparency: Every edge is explained and tagged as either EXTRACTED (explicit in the source) or INFERRED (resolved by graphify).
  • Capabilities: Users can ask questions, trace paths between two items, or explain concepts.
  • Outputs: The process generates three files:
    • graph.html: A browser-compatible file for clicking nodes, filtering, and searching.
    • GRAPH_REPORT.md: A report containing key concepts, surprising connections, and suggested questions.
    • graph.json: The full graph data.

🚀 Availability

Early access to the platform is open at app.graphify.com before the public v1 launch. The CLI can be installed and registered via the following commands:

  • uv tool install graphifyy (or pipx install graphifyy)
  • graphify install

#Graphify #KnowledgeGraph #AICoding #DeveloperTools

item.title: Workflow1111: A Gradio graph unifying eleven media pipelines with 73 nodes
item.description:
Workflow1111: A Gradio graph unifying eleven media pipelines with 73 nodes

A new Gradio workflow called Workflow1111 connects eleven media pipelines using a graph of seventy‑three nodes. It combines state‑of‑the‑art text‑to‑image, hi‑resolution fix, image‑to‑image, prompt‑matrix, VLM interrogation, detection‑to‑inpaint, ControlNet‑style annotators, background removal, PNG metadata handling, and image‑to‑video in a single canvas.

🔍 Overview

  • Eleven distinct media pipelines are assembled in one graph.
  • The graph contains seventy‑three nodes representing operators.
  • Users can execute any pipeline by signing in with a Hugging Face account or providing an access token.

🧩 How it works

Each node on the canvas wraps a single operator; the operator’s inputs and outputs become ports for connecting edges.

Operator kind Description (from evidence)
fn A Python function (e.g., prompt‑builder, post‑process metadata writer, local Lanczos resample).
model A model invoked through an InferenceClient (e.g., FLUX.1‑Kontext, Qwen3‑4B, ViT classifier, DETR).
space Another Gradio Space called on the Hub (e.g., AuraSR ×4, BRIA RMBG‑2.0).
dataset A row from a Hub dataset.

Typical flow for a text‑to‑image branch:

  1. Prompt builder (fn) adds style presets and cleans the text.
  2. Model node calls the chosen checkpoint via Inference Providers.
  3. Post‑process (fn) writes generation parameters into PNG metadata.
  4. Hi‑resolution fix upscales and denoises the output, then a refine step using a FLUX.1‑Kontext model returns a sharper, larger image.
  5. The same Kontext node can act as an image‑to‑image tab.

Detection‑to‑inpaint branch:

  • A DETR model finds objects, then the workflow splits: one branch draws bounding boxes locally with Pillow/NumPy, the other creates a mask for an inpaint pipeline. Only the detection call leaves the machine.

ControlNet‑style annotators (Canny, line art, sketch, luma‑depth, posterize) are implemented as plain NumPy fn nodes, each taking about half a second on CPU.

⚙️ Key details

  • Operator composition: 36 operator nodes total; 32 are fn nodes, and 22 run entirely in‑process without a network call.
  • Local processing: Drawing, mask creation, and Lanczos resampling happen locally; only detection, model inference, and Space calls require network access.
  • Resilience: Roughly two‑thirds of the canvas continues to work if the connection is lost.
  • Controls: Mirrors Automatic1111 txt2img tab – negative prompt, steps, CFG, seed, width, height, plus a model_id field for checkpoint selection.
  • Tag generation: A Qwen3‑4B model node produces a clean list of up to forty tags (e.g., “stormy sea, wet rocks, dramatic composition, low angle shot, volumetric lighting, ominous tone”).
  • Vision‑language: Qwen2.5‑VL can write a prompt from a night‑market photo; a ViT classifier returns scene labels with confidence scores.
  • Prompt matrix: A base prompt “a lone oak tree” is combined with four suffixes by a fn node, each sent to its own text‑to‑image node; a final node stitches the four results into a contact sheet.
  • No loop operator: The four text‑to‑image nodes sit side by side on the canvas.

🚀 Availability

  • Run any pipeline by signing in with a Hugging Face account or supplying an access token.
  • All operators are built from the same four operator kinds described in the previous post and the official guide.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates how a single Gradio canvas can orchestrate a wide variety of SOTA models and preprocessing steps without custom extensions.
  • Shows that most of the workflow can execute locally, reducing latency and dependence on network connectivity.
  • Provides a reproducible, modular template for building complex multimodal media pipelines that blend generation, detection, inpainting, and metadata handling.

#Gradio #Workflow1111 #AIpipelines #ComputerVision

Source: Rebuilding AUTOMATIC1111 with Gradio Workflow

item.title: Unlock the Power of Images with AI Sheet - Hugging Face Vision Tool
item.description:
🖼️ Unlock the Power of Images with AI Sheet

Analyzing your images with AI Sheets

🧭 TL;DR: Hugging Face AI Sheets is an open-source tool for supercharging datasets with AI models, no code required. Now with vision support: extract data from images (receipts, documents), generate visuals from text, and edit images—all in a spreadsheet. Powered by thousands of open models via Inference Providers.

We are excited to release a massive update to Hugging Face AI Sheets, the open-source tool for building, transforming, and enriching data with open AI models. AI Sheets leverages Inference Providers, which means you can use thousands of open models powered by the best inference providers on the planet.

The first version of AI Sheets made structuring and enriching textual content a breeze. Now, we’re adding vision to AI Sheets.

Images are everywhere—product photos, receipts, screenshots, diagrams, charts, logos. These documents contain structured information waiting to be extracted, analyzed, and transformed. Today, you can finally work with visual content directly in AI Sheets: view images, analyze them, extract information, generate new ones, and even edit them in real-time—all in the same workflow.

📖 Your Images Have Stories to Tell

Images contain valuable information—product catalogs, support tickets, research archives, receipts, documents. Now you can upload images directly or use datasets with images, and use vision models to extract, analyze, and structure the information inside them.

What you can do:

  • Describe and categorize images - Generate captions for product photos, classify document types, or tag images by content
  • Extract structured data - Pull line items from receipts, data from charts, or text from scanned documents
  • Add context and metadata - Automatically label images with relevant attributes, quality scores, or custom annotations

Just like text columns, you can iterate on prompts, manually edit outputs, and use thumbs-up to teach the model what you want. Your feedback becomes few-shot examples for better results.

🧾 Example: From Receipts to Structured Expenses

Imagine you’re back from a trip with a stack of receipts. Upload them to AI Sheets and create a column with a prompt like: Extract the merchant name, date, total amount, and expense category from this receipt

AI Sheets processes each receipt and gives you a clean table with all the details extracted. You can edit any mistakes, validate good results with thumbs-up, and regenerate to improve the rest. Export the final dataset as CSV or Parquet for your expense tracking tool.

Or maybe you’re digitizing handwritten recipes from old family notebooks. Create columns to extract ingredients, cooking time, and cuisine type—turning your personal archive into a searchable, structured dataset.

🎨 Generate and Transform Text and Images in the Same Flow

Need visuals for your content? AI Sheets can generate and edit images directly in your spreadsheet using AI models, keeping your entire content creation workflow in one place.

What you can do:

  • Generate images from text - Create social media graphics, thumbnails, or illustrations that match your content
  • Edit and transform existing images - Modify uploaded images or generated visuals—change styles, add elements, adjust compositions
  • Create variations at scale - Generate multiple versions or styles to test what resonates with your audience
  • Build visual content libraries - Produce consistent branded assets across large content campaigns

📅 Example: Creating a Content Calendar with Visuals

Imagine you’re planning a month of social media posts about healthy recipes. You have a spreadsheet with post titles and descriptions, but no images yet.

Create an image column with a prompt like: Generate an appetizing food photo for: {{title}}. Style: bright, overhead shot, natural lighting.

AI Sheets generates a unique image for each post. Not quite right? Create another column to edit them: Transform the image to have a rustic wooden background and add fresh herbs as garnish.

You can iterate on generation and editing prompts and try different approaches. Your entire content calendar—copy and visuals—lives in one spreadsheet, ready to schedule or export.

🚀 Step-by-Step Guide

Now let’s see AI Sheets in action. We will use open models to unlock the knowledge within handwritten recipes like the ones you could find from your grandma.

📤 Upload Your Data

We have a folder with photos that we can simply upload to the app.

The result is a spreadsheet like this:

⚙️ Understanding AI Actions

Each column in your spreadsheet can be transformed, extracted from, queried, and anything you can imagine using AI actions.

To see this in action, click on the overlay on top of any column:

Image columns come with image operations like extracting text, asking the image, object detection, colorization, adding text, and any custom action you can think of.

Text columns include summarization, keyword extraction, translation, and custom actions.

A prompt and a model define every AI action. Let’s see what we can do with our handwritten recipes dataset!

📝 Extract Text from Images

AI Sheets comes with a template to extract text from images:

The result of this action is an AI-generated column with the transcribed text. Let’s see an example:

For the above image, the extracted text is as follows:

1
2
3
4

MEMORANDUM: From To 1 Box Duncan Hines Yellow Cake Mix 1 Box instant lemon pudding 2/3 cups
water 1/2 cup Mozola oil 4 eggs Lemon flavoring to taste. Put in mixing bowl and beat for 10
min. and REMEMBER... for Quality PRINTING CALL OR WRITE Gatling & Pierce PRINTERS TELEPHONE
332-2579 22 YEARS OF SERVICE IN NORTHEASTERN CAROLINA

Not bad! But we see it has included printed text for the header and footer, and we’re interested in the recipe text. The reason this text is included is that we have used the default template for text extraction, which is as follows:

Extract and transcribe all visible text from the image, including signs, labels, documents, or any written content

Let’s now try a custom prompt.

Here is the extracted recipe details:

  • 1 box Duncan Hines Yellow Cake Mix
  • 1 box instant lemon pudding
  • 2/3 cups water
  • 1/2 cup Mazola oil
  • 4 eggs
  • Lemon flavoring to taste
  • Put in mixing bowl and beat for 10 minutes

This is great! But what about more complex images? By default, AI Sheets uses models with a good balance of speed and accuracy, but you can experiment with thousands of models. The above example uses the default vision language model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct.

Let’s test a SoTA reasoning model, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Reasoning, with a more challenging image.

Here’s the comparison between the models:

Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Reasoning

around. Then blend - Last sprinkle blend again Bake in large pan for 10-15 min. at 350. Let
stand 5 min before serving. in lg bowl combine meat, onion, bread crumbs 1/4 nutmeg & cheese -

50-60 min. @ 350 - let stand 5 min before serving

Both models produce very similar outputs, but with two subtle but important details (in bold): the temperature and a key ingredient: spinach.

🔧 Clean, Transform, and Enrich Text

Once we are satisfied with the extracted text, we can further transform and enrich it. We need to perform an AI action with the new column as follows:

We now have a beautifully structured HTML page for each recipe:

🖼️ Edit and Transform Image

Finally, AI Sheets integrates image-to-image models like Qwen-Image-Edit. This means you can run AI actions to transform and enrich your images.

For example, let’s say you want to give your recipes an old-looking style, you need to go to the column and use the B&W template like so:

Result:

📦 Export Your Dataset

Once you’re happy with your new dataset, export it to the Hub! You can export it to an organization, your personal profile or make it private if you don’t want to share it with the community.

You can check out the datasetwe have just created.

🔮 What’s Next?

You can try AI Sheets without installing or downloading and deploying it locally from the GitHub repo. To run locally and get the most out of it, we recommend you subscribe to PRO and get 20x monthly inference usage.

If you have questions or suggestions, let us know in the Community tab or by opening an issue on GitHub.

🙌 Credits

Originally posted at: https://huggingface.co/blog/aisheets-unlock-images

🏁 Conclusion

AI Sheets represents a significant leap forward in making AI vision capabilities accessible to everyone, regardless of technical expertise. By combining the familiar spreadsheet interface with powerful vision models, it democratizes complex image processing workflows. Whether you’re digitizing handwritten documents, creating visual content at scale, or extracting structured data from images, AI Sheets provides a seamless, no-code solution that leverages the best open-source models available.

The integration of vision capabilities into AI Sheets opens up countless possibilities for businesses, researchers, and content creators. From automating data entry from receipts to generating branded visuals for marketing campaigns, this tool bridges the gap between powerful AI models and practical, everyday applications.

🤖 Democratizing Data Science: How Amazon Q Developer is Revolutionizing Machine Learning for Everyone

🧠 How Amazon Q Developer Works: AI Agency in Action

At its core, Amazon Q Developer functions as an 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺—an autonomous AI that acts on your behalf. Here’s the fascinating part: the system combines a large language model (LLM) interface with a structured nonvolatile-memory block that retains critical information throughout your conversation.

The workflow begins with you describing your business problem in plain language. For example, you might say: “I’m a credit risk analyst at a bank and want to classify loan applicants as default or non-default based on their financial characteristics and economic indicators.”

From there, you can:

  • Select an existing dataset
  • Create a new dataset from S3, Redshift, SQL, or Snowflake
  • Simply upload a CSV file from your computer

The system expects tabular data with target columns (what you want to predict) and feature columns (data points used for prediction). For time-series forecasting, you’ll also need a timestamp column.

📸 See illustration showing the architecture of Q Developer data science assistant

What makes this system truly powerful is its dependency graph structure—each node represents a problem variable like problem_type, evaluation_metric, or target_column. This architecture helps the agent infer missing variables necessary for building your ML model.

🔍 Automatic Intelligence: From Data to Predictions

Once you’ve provided your dataset and described your problem, Amazon Q Developer takes over with remarkable autonomy:

🧹 Intelligent Data Preparation

The system automatically:

  • Cleans data and fills missing values
  • Encodes categorical features
  • Handles outliers
  • Removes duplicate rows/columns

Throughout this process, you can ask follow-up questions about your dataset (e.g., “What percentage of rows have missing values?” or “Are there outliers?”) and use DataWrangler for advanced analytics and visualization.

🤖 Sophisticated Model Building

Amazon Q Developer doesn’t just build a single machine learning model—it creates an 𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗲 of models including XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, linear models, and neural networks.

The system automatically:

  • Identifies the appropriate ML task type (classification, regression, or forecasting)
  • Suggests appropriate loss functions based on your needs
  • Conducts hyperparameter optimization (HPO)
  • Manages feature engineering

All of these complex processes are handled behind the scenes, without requiring any technical input from you.

📊 Transparent Results and Deployment

After training, you can:

  • Run inference on test datasets
  • Deploy your model as a SageMaker inference endpoint in just a few clicks
  • Access an automatically generated explainability report

The explainability report is particularly valuable, offering visualizations and insights into:

  • Dataset properties
  • Feature attribution scores (which variables matter most)
  • The model training process
  • Performance metrics

💡 Why This Matters: The Democratization of ML

The significance of Amazon Q Developer extends far beyond convenience. This tool represents a fundamental shift in who can access the power of machine learning:

  1. Breaking down technical barriers: Business analysts, domain experts, and other non-technical professionals can now leverage advanced ML without waiting for data science teams.

  2. Accelerating development cycles: What once took weeks can now be accomplished in minutes or hours.

  3. Maintaining quality: By using ensemble methods and automatic optimization, the system often achieves performance comparable to models built by experienced data scientists.

  4. Preserving transparency: Unlike many AI systems, Q Developer provides clear explanations about model decisions and feature importance.

For organizations looking to become more data-driven, this technology offers a path to widespread ML adoption without massive investments in specialized talent or extended development timelines.
